entries.land_description: (End of #10 Rd). We are two (sometimes more) lesbians living on 30 acres surrounded by hundreds of other acres of forest in central Maine. We are chemical free. We share space with Carol's 11-year-old daughter, 3 horses, 10 chickens, 3 ducks, 6 cats and 1 dog. We grow much of our own food.
entries.notes: Lesbians are welcome to camp on our land whenever and for as long as they like. They must be self-sufficient and carry all trash out and leave camping space as they found it. We have full moon celebrations on Sat evening closest to full moon every month - all lesbians welcome to share/join us. We have/are: housing/permanent structures, plumbing/electricity, camping space, woods, slowly clearing farmland, women living and working on the land.

entries.land_description: A sanctuary for women, plants, animals. I started homesteading on a ten acre piece of land tucked away in the woods of Central Maine summer of '81. Doe goats, cats, a dog and sometimes other lesbians have shared this homeland with me.
entries.welcomed_groups: new members/residents, girl children, nonlesbian women (maybe)
entries.notes: I carry my water, plant and preserve the food I grow in my garden and the cheese I make, heat with firewood I mostly cut myself, build with scrap lumber. We have/am: 2 housing/permanent structures, camping space, woods, farmland, women living and working on the land.

entries.land_description: Located between Albany and Binghamton, NY on Steiber Rd. Lesbian couples have stayed here and love the peaceful quiet. 30 miles to a lesbian support group. For now, my two college age sons are part-time dwellers, also dogs and cats. One spare bedroom so Winter is not best for staying.
entries.welcomed_groups: new members/residents, girl children (maybe), boy children under 10 to visit, dogs on leash
entries.notes: Please, no hard drugs, guns or heavy drinking. Bring your own groceries. Donations appreciated but not necessary. We have/am: old house, plumbing/electricity, primitive camping space with stream, lots of woods, possible farmland, woman living and working on the land.

entries.land_description: (near Woodstock). Laughing Rock Farm is safe space for womyn. Maintained as separatist land for 8 years (since '78), Laughing Rock (formerly Rowdybush) is a working homestead with goats, ducks, geese, chickens, cats, fruit, veg and herb gardens, lots of private (clothes off) playing and swimming places, solar greenhouse, and a trillion tons of rock. It is our belief that all womyn (lesbians or not) need separatist space for healing; we offer it, on short-term basis. The Wise Woman Center, offers herbal medicine and spirit healing workshops, intensives, and apprenticeships.
entries.notes: We have/are: housing/permanent structures, plumbing/electricity, camping space, woods, women living and working on the land.

entries.community_name: SENECA WOMEN'S ENCAMPMENT FOR A FUTURE OF PEACE & JUSTICE
entries.land_description: We are a permanent vigil for peace and justice outside the Seneca Army Depot, the largest nuclear weapons storage site in the world. We are an open, constantly changing, feminist community struggling to overcome oppression and militarism both outside our community and within it.
entries.welcomed_groups: all women who respect our commitment to non-violence and consensus process for short and long-term stays, new members/residents, girl & boy children, nonlesbian women
entries.notes: Work is done collectively, and all meals are communal and vegetarian. All permanent structures are wheelchair accessible, and there are chem-free spaces on the land. We have/are: housing/permanent structures, electricity, woods, camping space, women living and working on the land.

entries.land_description: (35 miles from Baltimore). We are presently 4 lesbians, down from 7 over the summer. We are in big transitions, and are hoping to focus our energies this winter to achieve some concrete goals. Right now it feels like everything is up in the air. Miscommunication is a common theme in our lives and we're struggling for ways to live harmoniously as a group instead of as separate individuals "tolerating" each other.
entries.welcomed_groups: new members/residents, girl children, nonlesbian women
entries.notes: We're not into drugs. We have/are: 5 buildings, conference center facilities, solar greenhouse, plumbing/electricity, camping space, woods (25 acres), limited farmland, a lot of gardens - 20 years organic, friendly neighbors, women working the land, an inactive group with hopes to revive.

entries.street_address: c/o Nan or Ruth, South Morgan Dr, Box 65
entries.land_description: (unger, WV). In 1982, construction of an owner-built, passive-solar home began and is nearing completion. We're musicians and sponsor women-only concerts every June and Sept as Rural Women's Productions. We run a consulting and woodworking business.
entries.notes: No drugs, moderate alcohol, smoking restrictions, bring food to share. We have/are: 1 house, 1 permanent structure, plumbing/electricity, unlimited camping space, woods, women living on the land.

entries.street_address: c/o Duffy Z Baum, PO Box 678
entries.land_description: (Located in rural Pittsboro, NC). The property is a mixture of hardwoods and pines with 3 fields and one finished house on 50 acres. I am interested in having other women build houses and live on the land. I am also open to selling 5-10 acres. There is a large, active lesbian community about 35 miles away in Durham. Herland is about 35 miles from Raleigh and 20 miles from Chapel Hill. Unemployment in this area
